0.headline: Tonbo Imaging India IPO GMP at 47% ahead of Rs 852-crore issue launch on October 15
0.heading: Tonbo Imaging India IPO GMP at 47% ahead of Rs 852-crore issue launch on October 15
0.intro: The initial public offering (IPO) of the Bengaluru-based Defence electronics original equipment manufacturer, Tonbo Imaging India, is commanding a strong grey market premium ahead of the Rs 852-crore issue launch on October 15.
0.body:
The initial public offering (IPO) of the Bengaluru-based Defence electronics original equipment manufacturer, Tonbo Imaging India, is commanding a strong grey market premium ahead of the Rs 852-crore issue launch on October 15.

According to market tracking platform InvestorGain, the grey market premium of Tonbo Imaging is nearly 47 percent on the morning of October 12. However, grey market premiums are unofficial indicators based on speculative trading and do not guarantee listing gains.

The company has fixed the price band at Rs 665–700 per share for the Rs 852.18-crore public issue.

Read Also: From struggling café to Rs 70-crore ice cream brand: How Narayan Rao built Bengaluru's popular 'Corner House Ice Creams'

The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The anchor book for institutional investors will open on October 14.

The company is offering 1,21,74,046 equity shares through an offer for sale (OFS), with no fresh issue component. At the upper end of the price band, the issue is valued at Rs 852.18 crore, implying a company valuation of around Rs 4,010 crore.

The IPO allotment is expected to be finalised on October 21, while the shares are likely to list on the BSE and NSE on October 23, subject to the final issue schedule.

Promoters Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar, Ankit Kumar and Cecilia D’Souza, along with existing investors including CEAQ Technologies, Timothy Guy Mitchell, Artiman Partners LLC and Ramesh Radhakrishnan, are among the shareholders selling their stakes through the OFS.

Since the IPO comprises entirely an OFS, Tonbo Imaging will not receive any proceeds from the public issue. The net proceeds, after applicable expenses, will accrue to the selling shareholders.

The IPO has allocated 50 percent of the issue to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 15% to non-institutional investors (NIIs) and 35 percent to retail individual investors.

Check IPO News Here

Investors can bid for a minimum of 21 equity shares and in multiples of 21 shares thereafter. At the upper end of the price band of Rs 700 per share, the minimum investment works out to Rs 14,700.

Tonbo Imaging reported a net loss of Rs 17.74 crore in the April–June quarter of FY27, while its revenue for the quarter stood at Rs 36 crore.

For the financial year ended March 2026, the company’s profit after tax declined 30 percent to Rs 50.88 crore from Rs 72.76 crore in FY25. Its reported total income fell to Rs 369.94 crore in FY26 from Rs 474.39 crore in the previous financial year, a decline of around 22.1 percent.

JM Financial and IIFL Capital Services are the merchant bankers managing the Tonbo Imaging India IPO.

About Tonbo Imaging

Incorporated in 2003, Tonbo Imaging designs and manufactures electro-optic and electronic systems for defence applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, handheld thermal imaging binoculars, targeting systems, missile seekers, fire-control systems and missile-guidance systems.

The company operates in the defence electronics segment, supplying technologies used in surveillance, reconnaissance, targeting and other military applications.

1.headline: Action returns to primary market; 9 IPOs worth over Rs 10,500 crore to hit Dalal Street this week
1.heading: Action returns to primary market; 9 IPOs worth over Rs 10,500 crore to hit Dalal Street this week
1.intro: The busiest day for the primary market is expected to be October 15, when five IPOs are scheduled to open, including those of Zetwerk Manufacturing Business, Bonfiglioli Transmissions, Tonbo Imaging and Sahajanand Medical Technologies from the mainboard segment.
1.body:
Activity is set to pick up in the primary market in the week beginning October 12, following a relatively muted previous week, with nine companies scheduled to launch their initial public offerings (IPOs), including six from the mainboard segment.

The nine companies are looking to raise a combined Rs 10,506 crore through their IPOs, comprising issues worth Rs 10,288 crore in the mainboard segment and Rs 218 crore in the small and medium enterprise (SME) segment.

Three IPOs are scheduled to open for public subscription on October 13, including that of mainboard company HD Fire Protect.

Mumbai-based HD Fire Protect, a manufacturer of fire protection equipment and systems, aims to raise Rs 712.3 crore through an IPO of 2.62 crore equity shares. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 258–271 per share.

Digital lending company Vaibhav Vyapaar and Kolkata-headquartered electro-mechanical projects and services provider Ravita Engineering Services, both from the SME segment, will also open their IPOs on October 13. The two companies aim to raise Rs 42.1 crore and Rs 116.05 crore, respectively.

Vaibhav Vyapaar has fixed the price band at Rs 51–54 per share, while Ravita Engineering Services has set it at Rs 105–112 per share.

Next in line is Fusion CX, a Kolkata-based global business process outsourcing and customer experience management company, which will open its Rs 702-crore IPO on October 14. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 275–289 per share. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 500 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of shares worth Rs 202 crore by the promoters.

The busiest day for the primary market is expected to be October 15, when five IPOs are scheduled to open, including those of Zetwerk Manufacturing Business, Bonfiglioli Transmissions, Tonbo Imaging India and Sahajanand Medical Technologies from the mainboard segment.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Together, these five public issues are expected to account for around 88 percent, or Rs 9,234 crore, of the total Rs 10,506 crore that companies plan to raise through IPOs this week.

Promoted by Amrit Pratik Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Bengaluru-based Zetwerk Manufacturing Business is the largest IPO among the companies launching issues this week. The technology-led manufacturing platform for industrial and consumer goods aims to raise Rs 5,012.3 crore at the upper end of its price band of Rs 143–151 per share.

The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an OFS of 14.45 crore equity shares worth Rs 2,182.3 crore by existing shareholders.

Bonfiglioli Transmissions, a provider of power transmission and drive solutions and the Indian subsidiary of Italy's Bonfiglioli S.p.A., aims to raise Rs 2,533.6 crore through its IPO at the upper end of the price band of Rs 558–586 per share.

Meanwhile, Bengaluru-based Tonbo Imaging India, a defence electronics original equipment manufacturer (OEM), plans to raise Rs 852 crore through an IPO comprising 1.2 crore equity shares. Sahajanand Medical Technologies, a Gujarat-based cardiovascular medical device manufacturer, aims to raise Rs 475.5 crore through an IPO of 1.38 crore shares.

All three IPOs—those of Bonfiglioli Transmissions, Tonbo Imaging India and Sahajanand Medical Technologies—comprise entirely an OFS, with no fresh issue component. Tonbo Imaging has fixed its price band at Rs 665–700 per share, while Sahajanand Medical Technologies has set its price band at Rs 327–344 per share.

Shellz India, a confectionery products manufacturer from the SME segment, will also open its Rs 60-crore IPO on October 15. The company has fixed the price band at Rs 170–179 per share for the issue of 33.5 lakh shares.

2.headline: Sahajanand Medical Technologies fixes price band at Rs 327–344 per share for Rs 475-crore IPO
2.heading: Sahajanand Medical Technologies fixes price band at Rs 327–344 per share for Rs 475-crore IPO
2.intro: Sahajanand Medical Technologies IPO | The public issue will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19.
2.body:
Sahajanand Medical Technologies, a Gujarat-based cardiovascular medical device manufacturer, on Monday announced a price band of Rs 327–344 per share for its upcoming public issue of 1.38 crore equity shares.

The initial public offering (IPO), which comprises entirely an offer for sale (OFS) by existing shareholders, will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The one-day anchor book for institutional investors will open on October 14.

The IPO share allotment is likely to be finalised on October 21, while the company's shares are expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 23.

The company is raising Rs 475.5 crore via initial share sale, and is looking for a market capitalisation of around Rs 3,500 crore.

The promoters, along with investors Samara Capital Markets Holding, Kotak Pre-IPO Opportunities Fund and NHPEA Sparkle Holding BV, will be the selling shareholders in the OFS.

As the issue comprises entirely an OFS, the net proceeds will accrue to the selling shareholders, and the company will not receive any funds from the offering.

The company has allocated 50 percent of the net offer, excluding the 2.5 lakh shares reserved for employees, to qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 15 percent to non-institutional investors (NIIs) and the remaining 35 percent to retail investors.

Click Here to Read all IPO News

Investors can bid for a minimum of 43 equity shares and in multiples of 43 shares thereafter. Accordingly, the minimum and maximum investments for retail investors will be Rs 14,792 and Rs 1,92,296, respectively.

Backed by Samara Capital, Morgan Stanley, Kotak Investment Advisors and Ashish Kacholia, Sahajanand Medical Technologies develops Class III and Class C/D medical devices, focusing on vascular intervention products, including coronary stents and balloons, as well as structural heart devices, including transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) systems and occluders.

The company's financial performance has been strong in recent years. Its profit rose 174.65 percent to Rs 69.1 crore in the financial year ended March 2026, compared with Rs 25.15 crore in the previous financial year. Revenue during the same period increased 18.1 percent to Rs 1,210.5 crore from Rs 1,024.9 crore.

For the April–June 2026 quarter, the company reported a profit of Rs 15.1 crore on revenue of Rs 351.6 crore.

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Avendus Capital, HSBC Securities and Capital Markets (India), and Nuvama Wealth Management are acting as the book-running lead managers for the Sahajanand Medical Technologies IPO.
